stories.title: The Lion and the Mouse
stories.moral: A small friend can be a great helper!

pages.text: Once upon a time, a big strong lion was sleeping under a tree in the forest.
pages.speakText: Once upon a time, a big strong lion was sleeping under a tree in the forest.

pages.text: A tiny mouse was playing nearby. She ran over the lion's nose by mistake!

pages.text: The lion woke up very angry! He caught the little mouse in his big paw.
pages.speakText: The lion woke up very angry! He caught the little mouse in his big paw.

pages.text: Please let me go! said the mouse. One day I will help you! The lion laughed and set her free.
pages.speakText: Please let me go! said the mouse. One day I will help you! The lion laughed and set her free.

pages.text: A few days later, the lion was caught in a hunter's net. He roared and roared for help!

pages.text: The little mouse heard the lion and quickly chewed through the ropes. The lion was free! They became best friends. Moral: Even a small friend can be a great helper!

stories.title: The Tortoise and the Hare
stories.moral: Slow and steady wins the race!

pages.text: The hare always made fun of the slow tortoise. I am the fastest animal! the hare would brag.
pages.speakText: The hare always made fun of the slow tortoise. I am the fastest animal! the hare would brag.

pages.text: One day the tortoise said: Let us have a race! The hare laughed, but agreed.
pages.speakText: One day the tortoise said: Let us have a race! The hare laughed, but agreed.

pages.text: The race started! The hare zoomed ahead very fast. The tortoise walked slowly but steadily.
pages.speakText: The race started! The hare zoomed ahead very fast. The tortoise walked slowly but steadily.

pages.text: The hare was so far ahead that he decided to take a nap under a shady tree.
pages.speakText: The hare was so far ahead that he decided to take a nap under a shady tree.

pages.text: The tortoise kept walking and walking, slowly passing the sleeping hare.
pages.speakText: The tortoise kept walking and walking, slowly passing the sleeping hare.

pages.text: The tortoise crossed the finish line first! The hare woke up and ran, but it was too late. Moral: Slow and steady wins the race!

stories.title: The Thirsty Crow
stories.moral: Use your brain to solve problems!

pages.text: On a hot summer day, a crow was very thirsty. It flew here and there looking for water.
pages.speakText: On a hot summer day, a crow was very thirsty. It flew here and there looking for water.

pages.text: At last, the crow found a pot with a little water at the bottom. But the pot was tall and the water was too low to reach!
pages.speakText: At last, the crow found a pot with a little water at the bottom. But the pot was tall and the water was too low to reach!

pages.text: The crow thought and thought. Then it had a clever idea!
pages.speakText: The crow thought and thought. Then it had a clever idea!

pages.text: The crow picked up small stones one by one and dropped them into the pot.
pages.speakText: The crow picked up small stones one by one and dropped them into the pot.

pages.text: The water rose higher and higher. Soon the crow could reach the water and drink! Moral: Use your brain to solve problems!

stories.title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar
stories.moral: Eating healthy helps you grow strong!

pages.text: One moonlit night, a tiny egg lay on a leaf. On Sunday morning, a tiny caterpillar hatched out!
pages.speakText: One moonlit night, a tiny egg lay on a leaf. On Sunday morning, a tiny caterpillar hatched out!

pages.text: The caterpillar was very hungry! On Monday he ate one apple. On Tuesday he ate two pears. On Wednesday he ate three oranges.
pages.speakText: The caterpillar was very hungry! On Monday he ate one apple. On Tuesday he ate two pears. On Wednesday he ate three oranges.

pages.text: On Thursday, four strawberries. On Friday, five oranges. On Saturday, he ate all kinds of yummy food and had a tummy ache!
pages.speakText: On Thursday, four strawberries. On Friday, five oranges. On Saturday, he ate all kinds of yummy food and had a tummy ache!

pages.text: On Sunday, the caterpillar ate one green leaf and felt much better!
pages.speakText: On Sunday, the caterpillar ate one green leaf and felt much better!

pages.text: The caterpillar was big and fat. He built a cozy cocoon around himself and stayed inside for two weeks.
pages.speakText: The caterpillar was big and fat. He built a cozy cocoon around himself and stayed inside for two weeks.

pages.text: Then he pushed out of the cocoon and he was a beautiful butterfly! Moral: Eating healthy food helps you grow big and beautiful!

stories.moral: Good things take time to grow.

pages.text: A little seed sleeps in the soil.

stories.title: The Little Red Hen
stories.moral: Work hard and you will enjoy the reward.

pages.text: A little red hen finds some grains of wheat.
pages.speakText: A little red hen finds some grains of wheat.

pages.text: "Who will help me plant the wheat?" she asks.
pages.speakText: "Who will help me plant the wheat?" she asks.

pages.text: "Not I," says the cat. "Not I," says the dog.
pages.speakText: "Not I," says the cat. "Not I," says the dog.

pages.text: So the hen plants the wheat all by herself. It grows tall and golden.

stories.title: Tara and the Moon
stories.moral: Ask questions — that is how we learn.

pages.text: At night, Tara looks up at the sky.
pages.speakText: At night, Tara looks up at the sky.

pages.text: The moon is big and round. The stars twinkle, twinkle.
pages.speakText: The moon is big and round. The stars twinkle, twinkle.

pages.text: "Mummy, why does the moon change its shape?" asks Tara.
pages.speakText: "Mummy, why does the moon change its shape?" asks Tara.

pages.text: Mother says, "The moon shows us a new shape every night."
pages.speakText: Mother says, "The moon shows us a new shape every night."

pages.text: Some nights it is thin like a banana. Some nights it is round like a roti.

pages.text: Tara waves good night to the moon and goes to sleep.
